claims.text: The initial refractory high-entropy alloy is a homogeneous, single-phase BCC alloy.
The initial alloy has moderate strength and limited ductility.
A minor addition of an ordering element combined with controlled non-equilibrium cooling will induce in-situ nanoscale B2 precipitates in the BCC matrix.
Full high-temperature solutionizing followed by controlled cooling can produce precipitates a few tens of nanometers in size.
The proposed processing will produce a uniform dispersion of B2 precipitates coherent with the BCC matrix.
The B2 precipitates will obstruct dislocation motion.
Obstruction of dislocation motion by the precipitates will increase yield strength.
Coherent precipitate–matrix interfaces will accommodate local stress.
Coherent interfaces will promote favorable dislocation interactions.
Stress accommodation and favorable dislocation interactions will improve ductility and delay localized failure.
The treated alloy will have a statistically significant increase in yield strength relative to the baseline single-phase alloy.
The treated alloy will have a statistically significant increase in uniform elongation relative to the baseline single-phase alloy.
Simultaneous increases in yield strength and uniform elongation will improve the overall strength–plasticity balance.
The beneficial effect depends critically on the precipitates remaining fine, uniform, and coherent.
Precipitate coarsening or loss of coherence may eliminate the anticipated improvement.
